# submission name:
opal_v1

# upload zipped `archive.zip`
[archive.zip](https://github.com/ccastillo1043/comma_video_compression_challenge/releases/download/opal_v1/archive.zip)

SHA-256: `bd9a47149b52a8f4986758e9274e509836bfa9c89f9b5cb069e90837eeb18400`

Size: `182,040` bytes

# report.txt
```
=== Evaluation results over 600 samples ===
  Average PoseNet Distortion: 0.00000688
  Average SegNet Distortion: 0.00029639
  Submission file size: 182,040 bytes
  Original uncompressed size: 37,545,489 bytes
  Compression Rate: 0.00484852
  Final score: 100*segnet_dist + √(10*posenet_dist) + 25*rate = 0.16
```

exact score `0.1591495384`

# does your submission require gpu for evaluation (inflation)?
Yes, same as [#135](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/pull/135).

# did you include the compression script? and want it to be merged?
Yes, and it is intended to be merged.

# is this submission competitive or innovative? explain why
Competitive: Yes. It achieves a score of 0.1591, with a 4.7 kB reduction from the next best submission.
Innovative: Yes. This submission changes only the lossless probability law used to code the frozen tokens of #135 by using online projector adaptive learning (opal). It decomposes the inherited five-class law into the rank-one maximal projector and its complement, learns only probability transport between those sectors, and preserves #135's relative conditional law inside the complement. All 49.4 MB of adaptive sector state is regenerated from the decoded prefix. Essentially, storage is traded for some extra runtime.

# additional comments
This submission is a lossless entropy-encoding upgrade to #135. It inherits its semantic renderer, HPAC predictor, carrier, frame selector, residual table, token representation, and reconstructed video without modification. #135 predicts one of five tokens at every position. This submission decodes exactly the same tokens, so PoseNet and SegNet distortion remain unchanged. Only the probability distribution passed to the arithmetic code is adjusted.

At most positions, #135's highest-probability token is correct, but its mistakes are not random - they recur in recognizable confidence bands, cells, temporal transitions, and causal neighborhoods. This OPAL model separates each prediction into two sectors: #135's preferred token versus the other four, and it learns how much probability mass should move between them. It preserves #135's relative probabilities among the four alternatives, retaining the strongest part of its learned model.

That correction is learned online from the already decoded prefix using 55 families of causal contexts. Encoder and decoder independently reproduce the same adaptive state, so no learned correction tables or weights are added to the archive. The exposed a redundancy in the previous model, so token stream falls from 114,706 to 110,022 bytes, and archive is reduced from 186,724 to 182,020 bytes. The entire gain becomes a rate improvement because reconstruction quality is fixed.
